page.overview:
What is Last Void?

The Last Void is a fictional "location" created by H. P. Lovecraft and E. Hoffman Price for their short story "Through the Gates of the Silver Key." Its relationship to the Final Void, another term for the Court of Azathoth, is unclear.

In "Through the Gates of the Silver Key," Lovecraft and Price refer to the Last Void as that which is beyond all matter, and reality - transcending "all earths" and thus by implication all parallel worlds, alternative histories. The Last Void is thus, in current physics terms, either the Base Reality - or complete nothingness incapable of definition.

In the context of the story, it is clearly something inspiring both awe and fear. The story deals with the annihilation of individuality among many other themes and so it is not inappropriate to see the Last Void as a true baseline in the writings of Lovecraft but also in the broader Cthullhu Mythos, beyond any individual versions of any of the concepts or creatures written about, and since it is also beyond the Dreamlands it forms a kind of hard boundary within which the entirety of all the expanded Cthulhu Mythos takes place. It is the end of all invention, as it were.

Whether the resemblance of the Last Void to the annihilation of the ego and consciousness in Zen, certain Buddhist and Hinduism beliefs and in Jungian philosophy is coincidental or not is unknown.
